rationale: bugs_open/311 (090 CONFIRMED 2026-08-18, run 8aa2e283): a planned tool section can be neither REUSED nor CREATED. store_generated_component decides regen-vs-create purely by 'does any base row hold the LLM-chosen function?' (WHERE function=$1 AND forked_from IS NULL). When that row belongs in practice to ANOTHER site (content_components has no ownership column), the store treats it as the row to regenerate and the field-contract guard then CORRECTLY refuses to strand that site's content_data — so no retry can ever succeed, and the requesting site builds, deploys and serves WITHOUT the section. Measured: remortgagecalculator.uk (a calculator site) served with no calculator, 3 identical refusals; loanzy.uk lost 7 of 7 tool sections, its served /tools/loan-comparison-calculator page has ZERO input elements at HTTP 200; loans-credit-health-check retried 7 times on 2026-08-18 alone. The ~140-domain finance buildout shares calculator function names by construction, so whichever site creates a name first currently owns it and every later site ships that tool hollow. THE FIX: before treating a function-matched row as a regeneration target, take a dependent census (page_components->pages UNION site_components -> sites); on foreign dependents, DIVERT the write to a fresh BASE row named <function>-<domainSlug(requester)> (deploy_tool_action's naming convention) with section_type = the REQUESTED section name — selector-visible, so the requesting page's rebuild links it and later sites REUSE it (the library heals itself at first collision). forked_from stays NULL deliberately: every section selection path filters forked_from IS NULL, and the template is a fresh generation, not the incumbent's lineage (this differs from RFC_036's fork remedy at TOOL level on purpose — there the fork escapes a partial unique index and the deploy path links pages itself). Own-site collisions and unknown-requester callers keep byte-identical legacy semantics; base+scoped both foreign refuses loudly. The regen UPDATE also self-heals section_type = COALESCE(section_type, requested). Session research REFUTED the bug file's fix candidate 2 (backfill section_type): plan_sections Path 1 already matches by function BEFORE the selector, so the backfill is a no-op for valid rows and converts the guard-dropped incumbents' not_found into a QUIETER selector_error degrade; the correction is recorded in the bug file, LANDMINES and WRONG_CALLS. A 090 on that refinement was filed (intake 1306e72c); its run failed on the fleet's Anthropic API usage cap and the intake sits at triaged for automatic re-run — the substitute first-hand verification is stated in the bug file (verbatim guard message on work item 3d775f99 naming incumbent 824e3309; measured absence of </section> in all three incumbent templates against sectionTemplateValid's Contains predicate; the resolution chain read end-to-end). Consumers named: component-creator workflow (only registered caller — its failed items start succeeding as creations), plan_sections/selector (gains new base rows, the library's normal growth path), check_unresolved_sections (its retry loop converges instead of livelocking), the incumbent site's lane (gains the guarantee that other sites' builds can never regenerate its rows), RFC_034 conversion programme (converts by id, unaffected). No new action input keys, so no RFC_022 optional-key budget movement. create_tool_component (RFC_036's writer) is deliberately left alone: that RFC is OPEN with the owner holding a contained interim, and its remedy differs for stated reasons.

plan.summary: store_generated_component gains site-aware storage-identity resolution: a new helper takes a dependent census before regen-vs-create is decided, diverts foreign collisions to a fresh site-suffixed base row that stays selector-visible (section_type = requested name), keeps legacy semantics for own-site and unknown-requester paths, self-heals NULL section_type on every successful regen, and records diversions durably. Mutation-proven sqlmock tests pin both write paths. Register entry CLC-020 ships in the same commit.

edits.rationale: The regen-vs-create decision needs the ownership view the schema does not carry (content_components has no site_id). Isolating it in a new file also keeps the diff in the heavily co-edited store action small.

The identity must be final BEFORE separateInlineJS writes the /tools/assets/<function>.js src reference into the template, so the resolution happens right after parseGeneratedTemplate; a diversion is logged AND recorded durably via LogActionFindings so the decision is queryable, not just visible in scrolled pod output.

The old inline existing-row lookup is replaced by the helper's results — the query moved verbatim into lookupBaseComponent with its 2026-05-06 is_active-ordering history note, so behaviour on the non-diverted paths is byte-identical. The version-number read stays where it was.

section_type self-heal: a manually-seeded row can carry function without section_type for ever (26 live rows). COALESCE so the 26 rows whose section_type legitimately DIFFERS from function are never overwritten; nullIfEmpty so an empty request writes nothing. Response additionally names a diversion so the workflow result is honest about the identity change.
edits.sketch:
result, err := params.DB.ExecContext(ctx, `
        UPDATE content_components
        SET html_template   = $1,
            input_schema    = $2::jsonb,
            js_content      = $3,
            is_dark_section = $4,
            render_mode     = $5,
            section_type    = COALESCE(section_type, $6),
            is_active       = true,
            updated_at      = NOW()
        WHERE id = $7::uuid
    `, htmlTemplate, inputSchemaJSON, nullIfEmpty(jsContent), isDark, deriveRenderMode(inputSchemaJSON), nullIfEmpty(sectionType), existingID)

    // ... and at the response map:
    if ident.Diverted {
        response["diverted_from_component_id"] = ident.DivertedFromID
        response["requested_function"] = ident.DivertedFromFunc
    }

plan.risks: 1) Library growth: each contested function name mints one site-suffixed base row — bounded at one per contested name (not per site), because the diverted row carries the requested section_type and is REUSED by later sites via the selector; reviewers should confirm they accept near-duplicate rows as the price of un-deadlocking (CLC-006 already records that multiple components per section_type are legitimate). 2) Census completeness: only page_components and site_components count as dependents; if a site depends on a component through another channel the behaviour degrades to TODAY'S regeneration semantics (guard as backstop) — never below status quo. 3) The globally-unique name constraint: a suffixed name colliding with an unrelated row's NAME fails the INSERT loudly (visible failure, not silent). 4) Requester identity is input_data.site_id — a caller not passing it keeps legacy semantics by design; check the component-creator workflow config continues to map the work item's site_id into input_data. 5) The diverted row's display_name derives from the suffixed function ('Loans Credit Health Check Loanzy Uk') — cosmetic, matches deploy_tool fork naming. 6) The section_type COALESCE self-heal writes the REQUESTED section name onto a NULL row during own-site regens — for a row whose intended section_type differed, the request vocabulary wins; COALESCE prevents overwriting any already-set value.
